Pulled, and no: tools are not deferred. Both adapters still load the whole catalog on every turn.

**Pull**

- The remote `jusprin-newui` had been force-pushed, so a plain fast-forward pull was refused.
- Your local tip (`589563ff99`) was exactly the old remote tip, so there was no unpushed local work. I reset local to the new remote tip, `d66d79ea5f`.
- The rewritten history replaces your three old commits with reworked versions (`eb45279cd5` approval removal, `577283e36d` skills-versus-tools doc) and adds eight more on top.
- The old tip is still reachable through the reflog if you want it back.

**Tool deferral**

- **In-app agent:** `tools_for` in [OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:69](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:69) builds the full function list and sends it with each request. The only filtering is availability (import permission, or a session that names its own tools), not on-demand loading.
- **MCP:** `tools/list` returns the whole catalog; there is no tool-search or load-on-demand tool anywhere in the JusPrin sources.
- **The doc says so explicitly:** [mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:474](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:474), rewritten in today's `c01b1ccae9`, states that both adapters load every registered tool on every turn and that measured numbers will decide when deferral is adopted.
- **What exists is the measurement:** [test_openai_responses_agent.cpp:487](tests/agent/test_openai_responses_agent.cpp:487) records the per-turn catalog size, with a tripwire at 40 tools and 48 KB, and the usage listener reports input and cached tokens.

**How tools are loaded.** Tool search is a capability of the configured provider and model. We declare it in configuration. The code never works it out from a model name or an endpoint URL. `OpenAIResponsesConfig::tool_search` takes one of three values:

- `None` is the default. The model gets the full catalog from the start, as ordinary function calling.
- `Functions` turns on hosted search over functions that are deferred one by one.
- `Namespaces` turns on hosted search over deferred toolsets.

Any model on any compatible endpoint can use any mode it supports, without a code change. Declaring no capability keeps ordinary function calling. It does not make the model unavailable. When deferral is on, three reads stay loaded from the start: `workspace_inspect`, `settings_search`, and `settings_get`. This is a starting policy. It is not a measured ranking of how often each tool is called. Printer and filament sessions keep their small catalogs fully loaded. MCP is unchanged, because MCP clients do their own deferral.

The app reads `tool_search` from the `jusprin_agent` section of AppConfig. The value is `none`, `functions`, or `namespaces`. The environment variable `JUSPRIN_AGENT_TOOL_SEARCH` overrides it. An empty value means `none`. An invalid value is a configuration error. Keep this setting with the model and endpoint settings, and update it when you change provider. There is no allowlist of models or endpoints. The app does not probe the provider at run time, and it does not retry a request with a rewritten catalog. This capability only selects the shape of the Responses request. Support for a different API protocol still belongs in that provider's adapter.

Every request still sends the complete catalog, in the same order. That includes `object_import` even when there is no attachment. Running an import without an importable attachment is still refused. A search never rewrites the `tools` array, so the bytes sent do not shrink. What is saved is the definitions that the provider holds back from the model's context at the start. The input tokens and cached tokens that the provider reports remain the authority on actual usage. The budget is 20 definitions per turn. Going over 20 does not block anything. It is the point at which we start watching the measurements.

**Deferral.** Deferral means the model first sees only a short index and loads a tool's full definition when it needs it. Use the hosted mechanism that the model platform provides. Never write our own mechanism for switching tools in and out. We checked the documentation on 2026-10-10:

- [GPT-5.4 mini's model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-mini) lists tool search.
- [OpenAI's Responses guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search) documents `tool_search`, `defer_loading: true` on a single function, and namespace discovery. It also says that loaded definitions are appended at the end of the context, which preserves the cache.
- [OpenRouter's hosted tool search](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/tool-search) documents `tool_search` on the Responses API as an alias of `openrouter:tool_search`, with `defer_loading`, across models and providers. At the level of documentation, this covers the DeepSeek V4 Flash route that the prompt tests use. ## Making deferral the default

The code change is small. What blocks it is that deferral has never been run against a real provider.

**How I would flip it**

- **Where:** change the default in `load_agent_runtime` ([AgentConfiguration.cpp:60](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:60)), not in the `OpenAIResponsesConfig` struct. An unset `tool_search` would mean `namespaces` on the built-in OpenAI endpoint.

**The live check behind the default.** On 2026-10-12 the `--live-agent` scenario ran against `gpt-5.4-mini` on OpenAI's endpoint, once with the full catalog and twice with `namespaces` (once declared, once left to the default). Each run makes four requests: a question answered from context, a request to copy an object with `plate_layout`, the continuation after that tool call, and a later user turn. All three runs passed every check.

| Request | Full catalog, input tokens | `namespaces`, input tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| First request, nothing cached | 7,115 | 2,175 |
| Request that calls `plate_layout` | 7,141 | 3,377 |
| Continuation after the tool call | 7,683 | 3,919 |
| Later user turn | 7,418 | 2,475 |
| Total | 29,357 | 11,946 |

What the runs show:

- OpenAI accepts the request shape: namespaces, `tool_search`, and `defer_loading`, with `store: false`.
- The model found a deferred tool. Its response held a `tool_search_call`, a `tool_search_output`, and then a `function_call` to `plate_layout` in the `geometry` namespace. The search and the call came back in one response, so there was no extra request.
- The continuation that passes the search items back was accepted. So was the later user turn, which replays the namespaced call from the app's own history without the search items.
- The first request was 4,940 tokens smaller. The estimate from bytes, at four bytes per token, was about 7,191. Trust the provider's count, not the estimate.
- Later requests were still served partly from the cache (1,792 to 3,328 cached tokens with `namespaces`).
